session.title: Soft delete users and restore endpoint

checkpoints.title: Add soft-delete core changes
steps: I added deletedAt field and lowered password minlength in the User model
I updated validations to accept 4-char passwords
I changed passport JWT lookup to ignore deleted users
I updated user service to soft-delete, exclude deleted users from queries, and add restoreUserById
I updated user controller to add restoreUser endpoint
I added a route to POST /v1/users/:userId/restore and updated swagger minLength entries in user.route
checkpoints.impact: Users will now be soft-deleted (deletedAt set) instead of removed; deleted users are hidden from lists, cannot be fetched, cannot authenticate, and can be restored by admins.
checkpoints.overview: This change implements soft-delete for users: the User model now records deletedAt. Services and auth flow were updated so deleted users are treated as non-existent for normal fetch and auth flows. Deleting a user sets deletedAt and removes refresh tokens. Admins can restore a soft-deleted user via a new endpoint. Password minimum length lowered from 8 to 4 to match new requirement.

flow.action: POST /v1/users/:userId/restore
calls auth('manageUsers') to authorize admin
calls validate(userValidation.getUser) to check params
calls userController.restoreUser(req, res)
asks userService.restoreUserById(req.params.userId)
forwards restoreUserById(id) to user.service
updates User.deletedAt = null (restoreUserById); queries default to deletedAt:null

notes.change: Lowered minimum password length message from 8 to 4 characters.
Password minlength changed to 4 and added deletedAt Date field (default null).
JWT user lookup now excludes soft-deleted users by checking deletedAt: null.
Query functions now exclude deleted users; deleteUserById soft-deletes by setting deletedAt and removes refresh tokens; added restoreUserById to clear deletedAt.
Added POST /:userId/restore route and changed Swagger minLength occurrences from 8 to 4.

checkpoints.check: Run the test suite or start the server. Try: 1) DELETE /v1/users/:id then GET /v1/users/:id (should 404). 2) GET /v1/users should not include deleted user. 3) Try logging in as deleted user (should fail). 4) POST /v1/users/:id/restore to re-enable the user.

checkpoints.title: Update docs and add explanatory comment
steps: I changed the documented password minLength from 8 to 4 in the auth route Swagger comments.
I changed the documented password minLength from 8 to 4 in the users route Swagger comments and added the POST /users/{id}/restore Swagger block.
I added a short explanatory comment in queryUsers explaining why deleted users are filtered (so they don't appear in listings and behave as removed).
checkpoints.impact: OpenAPI docs now reflect the lowered password minimum and include the restore endpoint; the user service code documents why queries exclude soft-deleted users.
checkpoints.overview:
This change completes the documentation and small clarifying comment for the soft-delete feature. It updates the Swagger comments so clients see the new password requirement (minLength 4) and the new POST /users/{id}/restore endpoint. It also adds an inline comment to the user service explaining why queries filter out deleted users.

These are documentation and comment updates; they do not change runtime behavior beyond the earlier code changes already applied.
